items.quote:
Elden Ring feels more like a wandering simulator than a Souls game

Let's start with the good parts.
1. Weapon variety is much better
FromSoftware really expanded the arsenal. There are thrusting heavy swords, flails, hand-to-hand techniques, and even something close to firearms. Weapons are also more customizable now, since Ashes of War let you change their special skills. This is one of the game's best improvements.
2. Magic was rebuilt well
Instead of the old split between miracles, sorceries, pyromancy and hexes, everything is now divided into sorceries and incantations, tied to different stats. Inside those categories you still have fire, lightning, holy damage, blood, gravity magic and other effects.
3. Guard counters are a good idea
You block with a shield or weapon, then press R2 to perform a counterattack. It hits hard and does good posture damage. As an innovation, I liked it. But in actual gameplay it gets old quickly. Many enemies attack in long strings, and if your R2 is too slow, the next hit interrupts you. Shields also do not fully protect you from status effects.

Now the bad part.
1. The game is artificially stretched
I dislike huge open worlds with enormous areas and few clear landmarks. You end up poking at walls and cliffs, trying to find a path, or trying to guess where the enemies are actually suitable for your level. In my opinion, if an open-world game lets the player go in any direction, it should also make sure the player can survive there. Elden Ring often does the opposite.
A good example is getting an Imbued Sword Key in Liurnia, activating a portal, and suddenly landing in Crumbling Farum Azula, where a couple of enemies can destroy you in seconds. For me, this gigantic world was the same kind of disappointment as Gothic 3 after Gothic 1 and 2, Dragon Age: Inquisition after the first two Dragon Age games, or Elex after Risen.
2. Bigger does not mean better
I tried to remember why I loved Souls games in the first place. Apart from the dark, gothic atmosphere full of despair, I loved the boss fights.
But in Elden Ring the balance feels wrong to me. In Raya Lucaria Academy, I spent maybe 30-35 minutes total on the bosses. The Red Wolf died on my first try, Rennala on my fourth. But I spent around three hours running around, falling from beams, looking for hidden corners, dealing with annoying ambushes, and trying not to use ranged weapons out of principle.
Now imagine the ratio of actual combat to "exploration" when you are running through the swamps of Liurnia. I do not want to spend dozens of hours simply wandering through similar forests, ruins and catacombs.
3. The game is not really built for exploration
I am not against every open world. CDPR made good ones. The Witcher 3 has an informative map with markers and points of interest. Cyberpunk 2077 improved this even more: the city districts feel distinct, and it is much easier to understand where you are.
Elden Ring is different. It is very easy to miss important content. If you fail to meet a certain NPC, or miss them and move too far in the story, an entire questline can simply become unavailable. This kind of design does not make me feel like an explorer. It makes me feel like I need a wiki open on a second monitor.
4. Too much copy-paste
Even in Limgrave, after exploring my first few catacombs, I already understood the formula. Enter, touch grace, see the locked boss door, run through the dungeon, find a lever, open the door. If you have seen one catacomb, you have basically seen them all.
Ruins are similar: clear the trash mobs outside, find the stairs to the basement, kill a boss or open a chest. Dragons and dragon-like bosses also blur together. Changing the breath color or damage type does not make them feel truly unique. There is much less unique content than the size of the game suggests.
5. The variety is mostly an illusion
Yes, there are tons of spells, Ashes of War and weapons, but many of them are either extremely situational or simply bad. How many Ashes are really on the level of Lion's Claw, Carian Grandeur or Sword Dance?
Some weapons are also unpleasant for regular play. Straight swords feel weak. Dark Souls 2 and 3 could be played comfortably with simple longswords. But here, short weapons often feel miserable against huge enemies. Giant bears constantly push the player model away. In Ainsel River, ordinary short melee weapons barely reach the malformed star creature. You need a bigger stick, a bow or magic.

Conclusion
I do not share the universal praise for Elden Ring. For players who enjoy wandering around, collecting things and searching every corner **** map, it may be perfect. But if you mainly care about boss fights and tight combat, they are only a small part of the overall experience here.
For me, Elden Ring is not a bad game, but it is a disappointing Souls game. I would rather play a more focused Soulslike with stronger combat and much less of this grindy wandering.

Massive, beautiful, and unforgiving. Elden Ring delivers one of the best world designs I have seen in a game.

The Lands Between feel enormous yet carefully crafted, encouraging exploration at every turn. Every ruin, dungeon, and hidden path seems to lead to something meaningful, rewarding curiosity and patience.

A remarkable experience that sets a new standard for open-world design.

items.quote:
Elden Ring is the culmination of everything From Software has done over the past decade-plus. The combat is refined, difficult, and rewards players who are willing to learn the systems. The world is truly awe-inspiring with bosses that fit the atmosphere seamlessly. Whenever you think you have seen the entire map, you stumble upon another area, and another, until you realize you are playing a game of such massive scale and grandeur that you have to put the controller down to digest it all. The soundtrack is beautiful and is so important to this game because it sets the mood for every area and boss fight. Walking through Weeping Peninsula with the Limgrave soundtrack is going to be what I remember on my deathbed. Contrast the soundtrack for Lichdragon Fortissax with that of Ancestral Spirit, two entirely different fights whose music matches the moment. The scale of exploration, combined with soulsborne combat, made for a first playthrough unlike any other.

Countless weapons and spells lead to a wide swath of playstyles that the player can choose from. The game does not give you anything overpowered from the get go but, with exploration and determination, you can obtain gear that matches the challenge that The Lands Between presents. Most of the armaments are viable and with many weapon types, there is almost too much to try. 

The bosses are the pinnacle of From's boss design philosophy. These bosses are no longer those of Dark Souls 1 through 3 which give you fairly large and obvious punish and healing windows. Instead, the windows are tightened and you are forced to learn each moveset to succeed, there are few lucky or cheesy victories to be had in Elden Ring. Elden Ring also emphasizes status effects and poise buildup, giving the player more of a reward for playing aggressive. Not all of the bosses are incredibly difficult, but those that are are thoughtfully designed and are unparalleled in games history. The setting and music during the Mohg fight, combined with the difficulty of the fight, make it one of the best From has ever concocted. Malenia was infuriating at first but once you get it, its one of the most fun fights in any game. I wish ER had a boss rush mode for this fight alone. Morgott's fight is easier but man, what a tragic character he is and his curved sword is the coolest weapon in the game. 

Elden Ring makes good games look like bad games. In the words of Dunkey- "if you can play this game and not feel some kind of emotion come over you, wipe yourself off man, because you are dead.

items.quote: From the moment you step out into the sprawling, golden-hued vista of Limgrave, Elden Ring makes one thing abundantly clear: this is not just a game; it is a monumental achievement in interactive storytelling and world-building. Developed by FromSoftware and directed by the visionary Hidetaka Miyazaki, in collaboration with George R.R. Martin, Elden Ring represents the pinnacle of the "Soulslike" genre, transcending its predecessors to become a universal masterpiece.A World of Boundless WonderThe Lands Between is perhaps the most meticulously crafted open world in gaming history. Unlike many contemporary titles that clutter the map with repetitive icons, Elden Ring thrives on organic discovery. Every ruined tower, shimmering Erdtree, and jagged cliffside tells a story. The sense of scale is staggering, yet the world feels intimate, filled with secrets that reward the curious and the brave. Whether you are descending into the star-lit depths of Siofra River or navigating the gothic nightmare of Stormveil Castle, the art direction is consistently **** Dance of Combat and ChallengeThe gameplay remains the gold standard for high-stakes combat. It is rigorous and demanding, yet fairer than ever before. The introduction of "Spirit Ashes" and a more flexible magic system allows players to tailor their journey to their own playstyle without sacrificing the profound sense of accomplishment that comes from overcoming a formidable boss. Each encounter with a "Shardbearer" feels like a mythic event—a desperate, cinematic struggle against gods and monsters that tests both skill and resolve.A Narrative of Mythic ProportionsThe lore of Elden Ring is a rich tapestry of tragedy, ambition, and cosmic horror. Instead of forceful exposition, the story is whispered through item descriptions, environmental cues, and the cryptic pleas of its tragic inhabitants. It invites the player to be an archeologist of a fallen world, piecing together the fractured history of the Golden Order.ConclusionElden Ring is a rare triumph that manages to live up to its immense hype. It captures the essence of adventure—the fear of the unknown, the thrill of discovery, and the glory of triumph. It is a hauntingly beautiful experience that stays with you long after the screen goes dark, solidifying its place as one of the greatest video games ever made. It is, quite simply, an essential experience for anyone who loves the medium of art.

items.quote: Elden Ring is absolutely insane in the best possible way. FromSoftware took the Souls formula and unleashed it into a massive, hostile, and breathtaking open world where every corner hides danger, mystery, and reward. The game doesn’t hold your hand, doesn’t go easy on you, and never apologizes for it it challenges you to learn, explore, and improve through persistence. Every victory feels earned, every defeat teaches a lesson, and every boss you overcome delivers a rush few games can **** combat is heavy, precise, and brutal, while the world and its lore are told in a subtle, intelligent, and deeply engaging way. It’s not just a difficult game it’s an experience that respects the player and redefines what an action RPG can be. Elden Ring is unforgettable.

items.quote: Facil y rapido, sencillamente, una bestialidad de juego y un GOTY indiscutible. Su punto fuerte es todo lo que no tiene que ver con la narrativa directa: el mundo está increíblemente vivo y el mapa es tan absurdamente grande que te recompensa por cada rincón que exploras. La libertad es total, permitiéndote perderte por horas mientras descubres que las posibilidades de builds son infinitas: desde magias espectaculares hasta ballestas, escudos y armas con habilidades únicas que te dejan con la boca abierta. El apartado de jefe vs. jugador es magnífico. Además, aunque use el motor de Dark Souls 3, la ambientación y el diseño artístico hacen que los gráficos se defiendan de lujo. items.quote: Elden Ring is a game of quality that we rarely see. The game takes everything good about Dark Souls 3 and turns it into an open world almost always for the better, however, I do have some issues with this game. Most notably is oversized bosses, there are multiple fights in this game where the boss is so large that you can hardly see any of the animations for their attacks while being close enough to actually attack them such as dragons, dragonkin soldiers, tree spirits, the elden beast, and fire giant to name a few. It's not that these large bosses are too hard, but getting hit by attack they you can't really see feels cheap and almost like a design oversight. my other complaint has to do with two handing weapons vs power stance, it's really not even a competition here, power stance is pretty much always going to be the superior option if you can hold the weapons without fat rolling. They did somewhat address this in the DLC by adding a two handed weapon talisman, but its still not as strong as power stance, requires a talisman slot, and you have to get at least a coupe hours in the DLC to be able to reach the talisman anyway so if you're staring a fresh character it'll be a long time before you get it. All in all I love this game and have spent hundreds of hours playing on both PC and PS5 and it's one of my favorite games of all time, I cant recommend this game enough to someone considering trying it out.

items.quote:
Elden Ring is one of the most overrated games of recent years, carried almost entirely by FromSoftware’s reputation and the built-in hype of the Souls franchise. Strip away the name, and what’s left is a mediocre experience — a dated RPG formula stretched into an “open world” that mistakes poor design for deliberate choices. In any other series, this level of clunk would’ve been trashed with a 3/10 score.

To its credit, the world itself is breathtaking, with stunning art direction, the fighting feels good, and the item pool is incredibly rich as every chest hiding something unique. But the game squanders that potential with endlessly recycled dungeons and bosses, a rigid stat and upgrade system that kills any sense of rewarding exploration, messy balancing filled with over-agressive bosses, and an inability to tell a compelling story. (Because lore is not story, and Elden Ring never bridges that gap.)

Beautiful and ambitious on the surface, Elden Ring ultimately feels hollow once you look past the hype.

The open world is a time waster. You're really just going from boss to boss. The things in between are either worthless enemies or rewards which, 9 times out of 10 are also worthless. 

That'd be ok if combat was good but I find it boring, especially coming from Sekiro. Mostly stay away from the boss or dodge roll until you get an opening. Repeat until boss is dead. Vastly inferior combat system compared to sekiro. People will just say git gud but what's git gud even mean in this game. I had a lot of trouble against an optional boss, ancient hero of zamor I think, so I left and came back much later and whooped it. I hadn't gotten any better at the game. I simply had better weapons and leveled up. So it did not feel satisfying to me. That's really the whole point of these games, the satisfaction of beating a boss, but Elden Ring just feels like a chore to me.

This game got endless praise so I've watched a lot of criticism videos hoping to find I'm not crazy for not liking the game. I think it's odd that many of these videos called it a great game or even a masterpiece with flaws. That makes no sense, a masterpiece to me means as flawless as one can reasonably expect. There seems to be a culture around this game that can't accept criticism. The only thing that is a masterpiece around this game is the marketing campaign that combined with the reputation of fromsoft, created a feeling of fomo and a degree of hype that led to its massive success.

items.quote:
From an artistic standpoint, Elden Ring and its expansion Shadow of the Erdtree are nothing short of magnificent. The Lands Between and the Realm of Shadow exhibit exceptional visual artistry, rich in atmosphere and filled with striking detail. Certain boss designs are genuinely original and imaginative, and the variety in weaponry, armor, and spells adds further depth to the game’s aesthetic appeal. Regrettably, this is where the game's strengths end.
The narrative is convoluted, fragmented, and overwhelmingly opaque. Understanding the story without resorting to external sources—such as lore videos—is virtually impossible. Rather than integrating its complex lore through in-game cutscenes or storytelling (as hinted at in the game's trailers), the game opts for a cryptic and inaccessible approach. The narrative feels more like a disjointed collection of abstract ideas than a coherent storyline—at times, it genuinely feels as though it were generated by an AI.
The repetition of content is also a major issue. There is an excessive number of enemies, with many reused throughout the game—dragons, in particular, are recycled to an exhausting degree. Caves, ruins, and dungeons suffer from near-identical design templates, creating an experience that quickly becomes monotonous. After exploring a few of them, any sense of excitement or discovery is lost.
Regarding the world itself, it doesn’t quite feel empty, yet it doesn’t feel alive either. It’s densely packed—but with redundant, repetitive content that fails to inspire meaningful exploration. The promise of an open world filled with wonder is undermined by sheer overuse of the same design ideas.
Perhaps the most disappointing aspect for me was the difficulty. Having completed all previous Souls games without significant difficulty, I found Elden Ring—especially its DLC—to be unreasonably punishing. Certain bosses are grossly unbalanced, and the overwhelming number of enemies only adds to the frustration. I was ultimately forced to install a mod just to make the experience manageable, something I’ve never had to do with any prior FromSoftware title.

items.quote:
Elden Ring is a master piece. Everything a souls born has been leading up to culminating into this marvel in game design. The amount of ways that the player is allowed and promoted to tackle boss encounters is beyond belief. Regardless of build, you are met with encounters where you will struggle and ones where you will roll. And if you find yourself spinning your tires you can simply move to a different location and continue there until you have grown in strength. This is the best addition in comparison to the Souls line because the bottlenecking no longer exists. The visuals on this game are worthy of immense praise. I say visuals and not graphics because the individual fidelity of the graphics is not ground breaking. However, the way that Fromsoft incorporated its art design into the game was flawless. I don't need to see the individual hairs on my character and I'm not worried about it when I'm presented with incredible sky boxes and creative weapon and character design.
Overall this game easily slides into my top ten best games ever list and don't expect it to fall out of it any time soon.
items.author: KaedynD

items.quote: Elden Ring isn’t just one of the best games I’ve ever played — it’s one of the most powerful works of art I’ve ever encountered, across books, films, and series. Calling it a “game” almost feels like an understatement. Every step tells a story, every boss fight is a true challenge. Its lore is so deep and mesmerizing…The sense of discovery is phenomenal. The fact that the game doesn’t force anything on you and gives you true freedom is a massive plus. Thanks to the build freedom, every player’s experience is unique. Whether you want to melt enemies with bleeding katanas or dominate the field with lightning spells — it’s all **** world feels like a living painting. Melancholic, eerie, yet majestic. With NG+ (a feature that allows you to restart the journey from the beginning while keeping all your levels and items after completing the game), the story goes even deeper. Normally, I feel a sense of emptiness when finishing masterpieces like this. But with Elden Ring, I didn’t — because it still has more to tell. I can still try new builds, live different stories, and even reach new **** music is a masterpiece on its own — it ties you to the emotions so perfectly. Elden Ring is a turning point in the world of gaming. I don’t know when we’ll witness something of this magnitude again.

items.quote: FromSoftware’s Elden Ring is a stunning blend of dark fantasy, rich lore, and punishing combat, set in a vast open world unlike anything the studio has done before. The Lands Between is a breathtaking, mysterious realm filled with secrets, dungeons, and deadly enemies around every corner.Combat is tight and rewarding, with an insane amount of build variety, weapons, and spells. Boss fights are intense and memorable, with some standing out as instant classics. Exploration is where Elden Ring shines brightest — no quest markers, just raw curiosity driving you forward.That said, it’s not perfect. The difficulty can feel uneven, especially for new players. The open world, while massive, sometimes spreads itself thin with reused enemy types and mini-bosses. Technical performance on PC and older consoles can also be hit or miss.Still, Elden Ring is an unforgettable experience, offering dozens (or hundreds) of hours of challenging and rewarding gameplay. It’s not flawless, but it’s a must-play for fans of deep, immersive action RPGs.

items.quote:
Elden Ring managed to please both Souls fans and open-world players at the same time. 

Starting with the open world, it brings a variety of biomes never seen before in the genre, and its graphics were pushed to the highest level possible for the time. 

The beauty of the game’s art direction relies on muted tones, contrasted by intense golden highlights, emphasizing the clash between the gray and the pure, the radiant.

Narratively, this choice also makes sense, since the central story revolves around mythical pantheons in a fallen world. 

The desolation of the map is structurally meaningful, although it does have some minor flaws, such as the relatively underwhelming rewards for certain discoveries.

Still, the variety of paths, equipment, rewards, and powers you gain over time makes up for the occasional frustration of finding a mushroom where you hoped to find a new weapon.

Combat is undoubtedly one of the strongest aspects of the game, not only because it builds directly upon the refinements from Demon’s Souls and is heavily influenced by Dark Souls 3, as many fans point out, but because the end result is a system that is responsive, challenging, and true to the franchise. 

Perhaps the hitboxes could be improved, but that is something to hope for in the next game. This title from FromSoftware brought a true refresh to the action RPG open-world genre, something we had not seen since the release of Skyrim. It sparked a new wave of Soulslikes and helped popularize the genre even further.

Some argue that this kind of game should offer an easy mode, but that would only take away from the way its mechanics reinforce the narrative. In fact, there is an easy mode, if you choose to explore thoroughly. 

The game constantly gives you the opportunity to discover alternate routes and encourages you to find your own path.Since Elden Ring was my first Souls game, 

I formed a deep emotional connection with it and ended up playing the rest of the series. I believe many players went through the same process, or perhaps even took the opposite route, starting with Dark Souls and ending with Elden Ring to avoid the gameplay gap.

Narratively, the game also brings depth and drama. The fact is that Elden Ring delivered a reimagined product, building on its strongest features and turning its previously linear maps into an open experience. 

While its balancing is often debated, the execution is flawless.I cannot fail to mention the incredible sound design. With perfectly fitting soundtracks for every major and even secondary boss, the mechanical and audiovisual quality of this game is simply outstanding.

The final result is an experience so immersive that every element helps you feel the weight of that broken world. And yet, it also offers breathtaking and unforgettable sights, reminding us that even in the darkest universes, beauty still exists.

items.quote: FromSoftware’s magnum opus **** boundaries with its sprawling, mythic open world. As a Tarnished seeking the Elden Ring, you’ll traverse hauntingly beautiful realms—golden plains, cursed swamps, celestial cities—each dense with secrets, dungeons, and godlike bosses. Combat refines Soulsborne precision, now layered with horseback skirmishes, stealth, and customizable Ashes of War. The lore, co-penned by George R.R. Martin, weaves cryptic grandeur into every ruin and NPC, rewarding curiosity with existential awe.Freedom reigns: forge a mage, barbarian, or hybrid, aided by spirit summons for brutal encounters. While the sheer scale can overwhelm (reused mini-bosses, occasional technical hiccups), the thrill of discovery never wanes. From storming castles under blood-red skies to unraveling tragic demigod sagas, Elden Ring is a masterclass in worldbuilding and player agency. A monumental, punishing pilgrimage—essential for adventurers craving wonder and wrath in equal measure.

items.quote:
This was my first 'Souls like' game. Get past the learning curve, find decent farm spots and most definitely research how to upgrade weapons/spirit ashes and you'll be well on your way to one of the most memorable gaming experiences of your life.

The game won't show you where to go or what to do. Keep a browser open with the Elden Ring wiki to help guide you along the way. It's free      
and super helpful!

You won't be ready to tackle every boss fight you encounter. Learn what works and what doesn't. If you're banging your head against a wall for hours, you're probably under leveled or not packing enough fire power. Button mashing won't work here. It's all about timing. Remember that you won't take damage while dodging! 

George RR Martin's influence is unmistakable. I really hope they make a movie of this game!

Not enough has been said about the absolute beauty of the landscapes and architecture in this game! Mind blowing! However, this game is not respectful of the amount of gaming time that you have available. Approach each session with a goal in mind in order to get your tiny increments towards becoming Elden Lord. Look at the wiki and watch YouTube videos for guidance. 

If I can do it, then so can you!

PS Malenia is optional, but worth it!

items.quote: Elden ring is the peak of what From Software can offer but in an open-world ****’s start with some clarifications first: the game does not revolutionize the open world genre in any way, but is rather Miyazaki’s take on the modern game's tendency and obsession with massive maps and games with dispersed content and emphasized player’s **** obvious goods of the game are stunning scenery and some of the best bosses you will ever experience, even more, it builds diversity and crafting, tons and tons of content, and much much-needed quality-of-life updates from previous **** how does the soulsborne formula apply to big maps? Some positives and some negatives:Lack of linearity can sometimes induce the player to progress in some areas not intended to be played at that stage of the playthrough, creating extreme difficulty spikes transitioning in uncannily easy content because you leveled up too quickly doing some harder content **** the other hand, the player is free to approach the game and different areas at their own pace, bouncing from place to place with the joy of discovery and not chained to the strict linearity of a classic Dark Souls.There are two things that I found very annoying: recycled bosses when It was not necessary – I would rather have fewer bosses, but all unique – and the horrendous job the game does at directing the player towards some of its best content.  A bunch of the hardest and most iconic areas in the game are completely optional and “hidden” from the player’s main path. It’s a shame that content made with great effort can be missed without looking at guides and playthroughs by a good percentage of the “casual” player base. Furthermore, Miyazaki does not disappoint and keeps the lore of the game completely marginal and a mere side effect of playing, and side quests without a guide are 100% impossible to experience fully; but I get it, FromSoftware games were never about the storytelling, but about the experience.Last but not least, player accessibility was never more emphasized than in this game with ashes of war, easier-to-play long-range builds, and summons. These tools grant their fun to all players, even to those not interested in a challenge. (I’ll let purists and casuals debate if the developers are going in the right direction with this choice).Still, even with its flaws, the Elden ring is a masterpiece that should be played not only by Souls hardcore fans, but all gamers that can respond to the call to a challenge, an adventure, or simply the joy of exploration. Play it.

items.quote: Прошёл elden ring (без dlc) на пк (на клавамыши). Помимо нового компа святой человек подарил ещё и elden ring, так что я прошёл его. Я большой любитель дарк соулс, однако был наслышан от людей, которым соулс от fromsoftware нравились, что они  предпочли бы линейные ds нежели elden ring, и что открытый мир был ошибкой, я понимаю о чём они, но с ними не согласен. Наверное, я всего 2 раза в жизни был ошарашен визуалом в видеоигре. Первый раз это rust на максималках в 2016 году, но там я скорее офигел от того какие технологичные ландшафты может процедурно генерировать игра. В elden ring же самый красивый дизайн окружения что я видел в видеоиграх, это невероятно 10 из 10. Ничего красивее я пока что не видел, хоть и какого-то принципиально технологичного графона там нет, всё чисто гениальный дизайн свихнувшихся японских мозгов. Боёвка такая же как в dark souls, у меня к ней нет претензий, ни к одной игре Бабадзаки у меня их не было (включая sekiro). Наконец-то решили позорные технические проблемы на пк, которые присутствовали в dark souls (в первую очередь пинок и другие элементарные проблемы с управлением), в целом игра в простых вещах, которые другие игры делали навыворот стала намного лучше, лично я не испытал никакого дискомфорта. Однако, я вполне допускаю, что игра может в этом плане доставить уйму проблем, просто так получилось, что меня это обошло стороной. Теперь спорное, камень преткновения elden ring – открытый мир. Да, я согласен с теми, кто утверждает, что с ним что-то не так, в первую очередь что я могу выделить: 1) Игрок не знает куда идти ( те пунктиры, которые выдаёт ему игра – ничтожны) это порождает в свою очередь массу проблем 2) Игрок пропускает море контента, которое потенциально хотел бы исследовать 3) Игрок приходит куда-то слишком рано либо слишком поздно, что во многом пропуск контента, 4) часть контента изначально вставлена чтобы быть ctrlc + ctrlv затычкой, чисто капипаст, чтобы побольше пещер/однотипных боссов было 5) из-за наличия открытого мира теряется надобность сражаться/ в целом взаимодействовать с большей частью врагов в игре, раньше в дарк соулс каждый враг – препятствие, а тут ты их и не замечаешь. Все эти проблемы, можно было бы решить, оставив при этом наличие открытого мира в том или ином виде. Мне наиболее толковым представляется вариант, подавать открытый мир небольшими сегментами, ну и пришлось бы обрезать капипаст в таком случае, конечно же. Боссы все кроме Малении не душные, Маления отдельный разговор, будь она обязательным боссом я бы снизил оценку, а так пусть будет. Очень надеюсь, что в dlc не решили, что Маления это была ахуенная идея и не понаделали такого же мусора, пойдя на поводу у дурачков, иначе это фиаско. Это первый souls, где мне интересны были механики помимо ближнего боя, и я их охотно использовал, раньше это была такая муть, что и вспоминать не хочется. Отдельно как проблему вынесу крафт, он невероятно бесполезный, причем ты постоянно поднимаешь что-то с пола, однако применения этому я дай Бог 2 раза за игру нашёл, худшая модель крафта. Подытоживая, я скажу, что несмотря на недостатки, мне игра понравилась ничуть не меньше чем иная часть dark souls, а может и больше, и я даже не против, если в соулс будет открытый мир, даже в таком виде в каком он сейчас, настолько мне понравилось – 8,5/10. P.S. Насколько я понимаю elden ring самая успешная коммерчески игра Бабадзаки, и fromsoftware хотят доить её до смешного, выпуская dlc через два года и коопные режимы спустя 4, или что там они хотят сделать, в общем, видимо, стыдоба какая-то пошла и дойка фанатов по полной.

items.quote:
Após concluir e platinar Elden Ring, posso afirmar com convicção que este é, sem dúvida, um dos melhores jogos que já tive a oportunidade de jogar. Elden Ring transcendeu minhas expectativas, especialmente ao demonstrar como uma história pode ser narrada de maneira envolvente mesmo quando não é apresentada de forma convencional. A integração entre narrativa e cenários, seja no aspecto visual ou temático, impacta diretamente a experiência de jogo, elevando-a a um nível excepcional. Cada batalha, escolha de estilo de jogo, e construção de personagens (como builds e abordagens estratégicas) foram projetadas para proporcionar uma experiência verdadeiramente única.

O aspecto que mais me impressionou foi a incrível capacidade do jogo de combinar variedade e qualidade. Não conheço outro título que consiga executar essa integração de maneira tão magistral. A trilha sonora, direção artística, design de cenários, criaturas e personagens não jogáveis (NPCs) mantêm um padrão extraordinário de excelência. Elden Ring não apenas oferece diversidade em conteúdo, mas também assegura que cada elemento esteja à altura da qualidade esperada de uma obra-prima. É uma experiência inesquecível, que define novos padrões para o gênero.

items.quote:
I've never been a huge fan of Souls and Souls-like games, but I've always been intrigued by Elden Ring and I was genuinely interested to play it. To my disappointment though, it was really lacking to me in many aspects. 

First, the game play, very average and lacking any innovation - it's fine for a Souls game but that's it, no new, interesting or cool mechanics anywhere, and no fun in discovering and mastering them, just lots of slowly dodging, parrying and hitting your foes - there are literally bugs in other games that are better than actual mechanics in this one; it remains undetailed, boring, slow, heavy and just not fun (I like to move and enjoy action-packed and dynamic game play that implements well the game's mechanics, I don't want to roll for hours around a boss and sporadically trying to hit it: that's BORING).

Second, the open world, which is potentially beautiful, with wonderful scenarios, but unfortunately is held back by being very inorganic, inconsistent and lacking in design and inspiration, with many badly placed, out-of-context elements (e. g. enemy fields and bosses/minibosses) and completely lacking basic features, like proper weather and night-day cycles (which is kind of there but only when resting in checkpoints); plus, the world lacks completely of any proper interactivity: everything is extremely static and unexciting.

Third, the aesthetic and overall design, very monotone and extremely boring, with no differences whatsoever between the environments, which are very nice, but not at all outstanding; everything is very grey and sad, which just makes this game all the more sad, boring and unfun.

Fourth, animations and details, which are fine, but also very rough and unrefined (and are all the same).

Fifth, the features, UI, and lack thereof, are either needlessly complicated, like the crafting of weapons and potions, or completely absent, like any kind of quest tracking system (which is fundamental in an open-world game), plus the game's UI is very badly designed, convoluted and unintuitive.

The only point I view positively is the overall technical performance, which is good for a game this big.
Other points I didn't mention are good enough for me to not complain.

Overall, is it a good game? Sure, but in my view it's far from being the huge masterpiece it's supposed to be, since it seriously lacks any meaningful innovation in game play, mechanics and aesthetics - if you like the Souls series and Souls-like genre, go for it, you'll likely be satisfied, but keep in mind that this game will never really get out of its niche and will never make it as a real icon and as one of videogame history's greatest.

items.quote: Elden Ring é um jogo quase impecável, com limitações que atribuo mais às restrições de hardware atuais do que ao design ou à execução do próprio jogo. A introdução de novos elementos de gameplay acrescenta profundidade e complementa a experiência de forma significativa.Ainda que minha avaliação não seja a nota máxima, algumas questões merecem ressalvas. Entre elas, destaco o fato de que certos itens e builds só se tornam acessíveis próximo ao final da campanha, o que limita a possibilidade de o jogador explorar plenamente essas habilidades ao longo do jogo. Além disso, encontrei alguns bugs que impactam a experiência, como falhas que podem prender o personagem em áreas específicas, muitas vezes resultando em morte. Embora essas sejam questões pontuais, elas afetam a fluidez da jogabilidade em alguns **** entanto, Elden Ring é merecedor dos prêmios de Jogo do Ano que conquistou, e compartilho da opinião de que é um título que redefine o gênero e proporciona uma experiência incomparável.

Short review. i have 65 hours on my playthrough.

What a rule-breaking game this is! your expectations of games will be a little changed after experiencing the Elden Ring. I both love and hate this game, it requires patience, practice, and looking to others for help.      The main game is puzzlingly massive (map, enemies, and weapons) although it is very difficult, this game is very rewarding when things go right. 
     There is frustration and rage included in your playthrough, but after some time and a re-think you come back around and think of smarter and more sensible ways of progressing through the maze of bosses.      
     This game is nothing like open worlds from Ubisoft, Bethesda, Obsidian. It is more related to Zelda BOTW but has a more serious darker setting.      

Everyone should play this, and everyone will likely experience the highs and lows of this game.

items.quote:
Massively overrated and disappointing for any Dark Souls fan. I had high hopes but the DLC strengthens my opinion on this game. Fromsoft took everything bad from the previous games mindlessly put it here. They absolutely didn't learn from their mistakes. The fairness of the bosses isn't a point anymore. They're far too fast, it's like they've tried to make another Sekiro-like with parry based combat but either forgot that half-way through or someone accidentally added any bosses past a certain point for a scrapped game here (1 of the bosses actually is a scrapped boss from sekiro which makes this theory that much believable). The worst part of the community is they will 100%  avoid this criticism and just say "git gud". And I have, I've loved every other fromsoft game for it's difficulty, here it's just **** thrown together to make a hard game. Some moves straight-up cannot be dodged, mostly combos that are followed multiple times too fast for the medium-roll to work so you always end up getting hit 1-2 times no matter how good you are. Some of the grab moves one-shot so you wait there for a good 5-10 seconds for the animation to end watching it eat through your health like nothing. They didn't bother play-testing. The moves are awfully telegraphed so you have absolutely no idea what the boss is doing until you get hit. The game is bloated to the point that it feels like a slog.
-Stupidly large locations with no points of interests.
-Reused bosses. If you see a boss in an open arena it has 5 versions somewhere elsewhere.
-Reused dungeons. They all feel the same with maybe 4 different gimmicks that constantly repeat themself.
-Reused enemies. Because why would they bother making every location unique rather than favoring quantity over quality.
The developers didn't even bother to not make this look like a cashgrab. Quantity over quality is the best way to put it. Disappointing.

items.quote:
One of the greatest games I've every played, and in my opinion FromSoftware's best. Elden Ring is packed with unique characters and quests, beautifully crafted environments ranging from the ruins of Limgrave to the awe-inspiring Crumbling Farum Azula, and wonderful sets of bosses and themes that no other game can truly compare to.

Many of the low reviews call this game a copy of prior Souls titles, too empty, or too difficult. I argue these are made in bad faith. It's expected that a new Soulslike will be like... prior Souls games. Who could have guessed? And this discounts the insane overhaul that incantations and sorceries got, making them miles better than prior titles. Additionally, Ashes of War and summoning spirits are new mechanics that add a wonderful level of variety to the combat system. Being able to easily shape a weapon into a faith-based weapon via an Ash of War and a whetstone makes build crafting far more versatile than in prior games and makes combat all the more interesting. 

As for the world being too empty, this is simply false or pure rage baiting. The world is expansive, yes, but it is full of unique discoveries and wonderful little quests. In the areas of the map that are truly empty with nothing to obtain or nothing to fight, I find it particularly freeing to roam on Torrent without the fear of being attacked by an unexpected enemy. Now that I'm on NG+, there's a particular risk of getting hit by an enemy that I'm not fully prepared. The breath of fresh air allows me to think and plan on where I want to go next. 

Finally, for the complaints of difficulty. This is a bit of a no-brainer. Elden Ring is not difficult unless you make it so. Struggling to kill a boss? Go to a different area, explore, and raise your rune level. That didn't help? Begin using summons. That didn't work? Feel free to respec your character to the most broken build imaginable. Elden Ring gives you many more chances to respec off the bat than in prior games such as Dark Souls 3. The larval tears are a wonderful addition and allow the player to, in a single playthrough, respec 10+ times! People often complain that they "don't want to change their build they've been using the whole game". I can sorta understand this sentiment but it falls short considering the insane variety Elden Ring provides. Are you telling me out of all of the different weapon types (not to mention remembrance weapons), ashes of war, incantations/sorceries, and status builds (e.g., blood build vs. poison build) you aren't willing to change a single thing? I've seen people go as far to complain about having to equip a shield. Why is this a problem? You're telling me you aren't willing to change your build at all... in an action RPG? To top it all off, if you really are struggling that hard, especially in the latter half of the game, just use the Mimic Tear with busted incantations and a hyper armor build, and watch the boss crumble in the next few attempts.

People complain too easily. I feel that most negative reviews are people who just want to hate on the game that is nigh superior in every way to past titles. The last glaring elephant in the room is the performance concerns. This I don't think was a large enough issue to warrant lowering my vote from a 10. Although I definitely experienced these issues, it made up for less than ~5% of my deaths. In other words, out of 20 deaths, maybe a single one is from a performance issue. People complain about Elden Ring performance when it generally runs at 40+ FPS perfectly fine while their favorite title, the beloved Bloodborne, is locked at 30 FPS even on the PS5 due to the game's design. The irony.

The quests are interesting but still maintain the mystique of prior games. It's easy to miss something important, but I like that in the Souls formula. Players come from similar exploratory games such as Breath of the Wild and expect to have a quest guide tell them always where to go and where to look, but that has never been the purpose of Souls games. It's up to the player's dedication, intuition, and perseverance to explore the world and complete quests as they see fit. If you have a problem with that, don't laude past FromSoftware titles that do the same thing but at a smaller scale. It really isn't that different. 

All in all this game will eat your time away and is full of wonder. The quests, environment, bosses, and all are some of FromSoftware's best, only rivaled by the Lovecraftian design in Bloodborne. If you can stomach the growing pains of getting into a new FromSoftware title and a rare FPS drop now and then, try this on for size, and let it change your perspective on modern action RPGs.

items.quote:
Elden Ring is the most epic, most ambitious game I have ever played. I think this game goes beyond a recomendation.

I beat this game and all of its bosses (that didn’t regard a secret quest line concerning a 4 handed person that I didn’t find on my entire play through) with a standard build without looking anything up. I did not use summons or take any help. I played through with a strength build like I always have.

There has been some controversy around the game’s difficulty but I liked that it is the hardest of souls games. These games have always revolved around understanding enemy behavior and animations. This game takes that and cranks it up to 11. I never felt like anything was impossible and I even beat Malenia at level 120 in 3.5 hours. (which is a lot but it’s an optional boss so I never needed to get stuck)

This is the most beautiful game I have ever played. Every place just feels like I am stepping into a whole new world. The exploration is insanely fun and rewarding. You explore for weapons and levels and then use that in the legacy dungeons. Some people have said that the double battles are stupid and that reusing bosses is lazy. I have to agree with that to some extent but honestly you can always skip bosses like these. I know I did it a few times and I came back if I needed xp. This is true until you get to the Godskin duo.

Godskin duo was not the worst thing it the world. You have to hide behind pillars and use the surroundings as well as you can. You can often posture break or get good hits in one of them while the other is behind. You always have to keep your guard up and be ready to dodge. It is harder but I don’t believe it’s that bad. It’s like a C-tier fight to me. Just really basic and needs some good use of the arena.

Overall I don’t agree with the many criticisms that the game’s difficulty has gotten and I also think that the game’s overall quality is exceptionally high. I know some won’t agree with me but I am fine with that. I loved this game.
items.author: Somebody1

items.quote: I loved dark souls 1 and 3.I heard the great reviews of this game calling it the first half of ds1 combined with the base game of ds3 and open world of (my favourite game) botw, finally got it running on my pc and thought that this would be the best game I had ever played, it’s not. I am 17 hours in and just reached the Main atlas plateau and cannot continue.I will first try to sing this game some praises. I love the art style, graphics, varying builds (which I thought was lacking in ds3), the vast amount of weapon types, the boss runbacks and some bosses move sets, but I just don't like the game **** biggest gripes I have of Elden ring (in descending order) is the open world, repeating bosses/ enemies and the balances. To me Elden ring’s open world lacks the same charm as botw’s does, it feels like dark souls 1 but bigger, this may sound like a good thing, but the scale just exacerbates the flaws. In ds1 I always felt like I knew where I was going and why I was going there and even if I went somewhere where I wasn't supposed to, I could do or learn something substantial. An example of this is where you may find yourself walking to the graveyard and then potentially further into the catacombs like I did but it’s completely obvious that you don't need to be there because of the fat ass in your face staircase  leading to the undead burg Infront of  firelink shrine, in Elden ring I had no idea where or why I was going anywhere after Margit because of the massive scale and many paths. In ds1 it was either go to new londo or graveyard and realize you're too low level and go to undead burg yet because of the massive open world in Elden ring there are so many alternative paths that can be taken leading to me just not knowing where to go at all and not being able to perfectly remember the interconnected map like in ds1, there is just so many places to go yet there is a defined way you must play the game to open gates to progress ( unlike in breath of the wild where if you don't want to defeat the great divine beasts you can just fight Ganon and finish the game in around an hour if you're good enough which I loved) For me this makes it feel as if the overworld in Elden ring is just a facilitator to farming and levelling up but there are some methods of farming that are just superior to all the others so why not just do that. I also don't particularly like the "if you see it you can get to it" approach of the game, whilst this might be true like in botw , the difficulty of souls type games less incentivises me to explore that much due to losing runes but that isn't particularly detrimental to the explorational experience as I can just git gud or run past the enemies. The bigger, probably needy and whiny, complaint I have about it is that there are places that I don’t know how to get to. By this I mean that I will see something, for example the big mountain at liurnia, and try for so long to get to the top of it just to find out that apparently that’s a late game area and I can’t get there yet. So, what's the point of making it an open world game if I can’t get somewhere? This is probably a really nit-picky critique, but I feel as if it’s a valuable one because the constant "oh I need to get here but I can’t" situation is much more prevalent here than in botw or totk where I can just climb or make something to get somewhere making the Zelda open world feel like a constant puzzle, but the Elden ring feels like there are massive barriers. The repeating bosses also leads to a less magical experience when playing these games. Just like ds1 this game has repeating bosses but where the bosses in ds1 become normal enemies to show you how powerful you have become (taurus demon and Capra demon in demon runes) Elden ring just puts them in again and again. I am no longer put in awe of seeing these large spectacles of huge dragons or terrifying beasts that I can learn I'm just bored and want to get to the next proper mainline boss, which I do admittedly think (apart from some **** 1 shot moves) do very well, (Margit being probably my 3rd favourite souls’ boss after sister Friede and Gael).I guess how I feel about this game is that I was promised the first half of ds1 with the boss quality of ds3 and open world of botw but so far, I feel as if I have gotten the 2nd half of ds1 with the open world of Minecraft and a few amazing bosses

items.quote: Elden Ring, the much-anticipated collaboration between FromSoftware and George R.R. Martin has taken the gaming world by storm. As a long-time fan of the Soulsborne series, I approached Elden Ring with both excitement and trepidation, wondering if it could possibly live up to the monumental expectations. What I found was a game that not only met those expectations but transcended them, delivering an experience that is as profoundly moving as it is challenging.From the moment you step into the Lands Between, it’s clear that Elden Ring is a labor of love. The world is vast and meticulously crafted, with every region telling its own story through environmental details and carefully placed lore items. George R.R. Martin’s influence is palpable in the rich tapestry of history and mythology that underpins the game. The narrative unfolds in layers, encouraging players to explore and piece together the intricate puzzle of the world’s past and present. This method of storytelling, a hallmark of FromSoftware’s games, reaches new heights here, blending mystery with revelation in a way that is deeply satisfying.Elden Ring’s gameplay is a masterful evolution of the Soulsborne formula. The combat is as tight and demanding as ever, requiring precision, strategy, and adaptability. What sets Elden Ring apart is its open-world design, which offers unprecedented freedom and encourages exploration. The addition of the Spectral Steed, Torrent, transforms traversal, allowing players to cover vast distances swiftly and engage in mounted combat. This innovation adds a dynamic layer to the already rich combat system, making encounters feel fresh and **** game’s difficulty is a topic of much discussion, but it’s worth noting that Elden Ring provides a variety of tools to aid players. The summoning system, which allows for cooperative play, is more accessible than ever, and the inclusion of Spirit Ashes provides an additional layer of strategy. These elements make the game more approachable without sacrificing the core challenge that fans cherish.Visually, Elden Ring is breathtaking. The art direction is nothing short of spectacular, with each area offering distinct and unforgettable aesthetics. From the hauntingly beautiful ruins of Limgrave to the eerie majesty of the Erdtree, the game is a feast for the eyes. The attention to detail is astounding, with every nook and cranny packed with secrets waiting to be **** audio design is equally impressive. The score, composed by Yuka Kitamura and Tsukasa Saitoh, perfectly complements the game’s atmosphere, ranging from hauntingly melancholic to triumphantly epic. Sound effects are meticulously crafted, enhancing the immersion and making every action feel weighty and significant.Elden Ring offers deep character customization, allowing players to tailor their experience to their preferred playstyle. The range of available weapons, spells, and abilities is vast, providing a level of flexibility that is unmatched. The character progression system is intuitive yet deep, rewarding experimentation and thoughtful planning. This depth extends to the game’s NPCs, whose stories and quests add layers of meaning and consequence to the player’s **** narrative of Elden Ring is a dark and captivating tale of ambition, loss, and redemption. It explores themes of power, corruption, and the cyclical nature of history with a poignancy that is rare in video games. The characters you meet are complex and multifaceted, their fates intertwined with the larger narrative in ways that are often surprising and moving. The game’s ending, or rather endings, are thought-provoking and offer a sense of closure that is both satisfying and open to interpretation.Elden Ring is a triumph, a game that pushes the boundaries of what an open-world RPG can be. It seamlessly blends FromSoftware’s signature gameplay with a richly detailed world and a narrative that resonates on a deeply emotional level. The result is a game that is not only a joy to play but also a profound experience that stays with you long after the credits **** an era where many games are content to follow established formulas, Elden Ring dares to innovate, to challenge, and to inspire. It is a testament to the power of video games as an art form and a reminder of why we fell in love with gaming in the first place. Whether you are a veteran of the Soulsborne series or a newcomer to FromSoftware’s worlds, Elden Ring is a journey that you will not want to miss.

items.quote:
If this game had more development time, I truly believe it would be perfect. Unfortunately due to what I assume are either poor creative descisions or pressure to release on time, there are some flaws that make it impossible to a rate 10/10.

My first issue is the multitude of poorly made, unfair and... (for lack of a better term) **** duo boss fights. Most of these involve two normal enemies or bosses being shoved into a room with no AI tweaks. This makes balancing the two while making your own attacks incredibly annoying and unfair. I believe this was due to lack of development time, so I fault the publishers more than the developers.

My 2nd complaint is the performance (I know, low hanging fruit). Fromsoftware has a history of poor optimisation but Elden Ring is horrible in this regard. The only real way to get a consistent 60fps is to run on the lowest possible settings unless you're running a 4090ti. Normally I don't mind a few little frame drops but the game also likes to crash... very frequently. Especially at loading screens. And then they add ray tracing despite this?

My 3rd complaint is EasyAntiCheat. That is all. Nobody likes EasyAntiCheat.

items.quote:

The DNA is there, of course, but I constantly found just a little something missing. Upon finishing the game my thought was "Have I become a Dark Souls purist? Would I have had more fun without summons", etc. This is by far the easiest Souls game that FromSoft have put out. I do think part of this stems from the fact that if you do practically any amount of exploring, you will get overleveled. The result of this was I never got any moment of triumph from killing a boss as I killed practically every boss I encountered in 1-3 tries, including the final boss. I also ran into the problem of doing most of my lore homework by reading descriptions and what-not, but I still had little idea what was going on, and so this hurt my enjoyment of the game somewhat significantly. So while there's a ton of different builds to play with, plenty of places to explore, and lots of bosses to fight, I left this game feeling empty. I don't wish to review this as negative as it's still a solid game, I may have just inaccurately set my expectations, and was disappointed when they weren't met.

items.quote:
Elden Ring is an absolutely amazing game. It is a fresh breath of air in an oversaturated Open World RPG market. 

With hundreds of weapons and spells to use, as well as new mechanics such as the ability to perform a true jump, and guard countering, Elden Ring also feels incredibly fresh for returning Souls players.

items.quote:
A fantastic successor to the Dark Souls franchise, offering a huge open world, countless weapons, spells and incarnations, as well as the familiar great story, locations and boss encounters.
A new addition is an optional ghost summon mechanic, that can assist in most boss fights and harder open world sections, so people who might struggle with the steep learning curve or looking for a more casual approach, might find themselve satisfied.

Sadly I was left feeling, that the game being published a few months to early. The damage and resistance mechanics can be inconsistent and confusing, some items drops appear to be placeholder locations, while dungeons and monsters are sometimes copy-pasted over the map without rhyme or reason.
The typical FromSoftware approach to tell a story through vage NPC dialogs without quest logs or map markers in an open world, can let you miss out on some great side journeys, especially by taking longer breaks mid playthrough.

That being said, there is an active modding scene, that could offer solutions and the game is definitly worth its price!

items.quote:
I spent about 150 hours with this game on PS5 when it originally released. I absolutely hate Souls games, so Elden Ring had a steep learning curve which I fought through, and then eventually ended up thoroughly enjoying it. I saw the DLC was coming out, decided to give it a shot on my Steam Deck, and now I'm already 50 hours in a second time, just two years later. 

This game is a masterpiece. The gameplay itself is extremely hard to digest, especially at first, but once it connects, it makes for an experience that few other games pull off. My first time with the game I thought the combat was stupid, but I eventually just ended up accepting it as I ran through the rest of the game. My second time with the game, I am far more appreciative of the skill that combat requires out of you. The second time around, I am enjoying playing around with the builds a lot more. Its a very thick combat and build system, but once you digest it, you appreciate the intricacy of it all. I still find the exploration of the game to be the defining characteristic. The game provides you with minimal guidance, and lets you loose into the world. Due to the difficulty and learning curve, there is a lot of trial and error in the exploration as well. Even on my second playthrough I stumble into an area that is way too difficult for me, so I am forced to either push through it or wander the other direction. I appreciate how there is little guidance, because it creates this feeling where you aren't in any hurry to experience the world - this is something that most games struggle with today. There is minimal HUD, minimal dialogue, minimal direction, you just wander. There are times I wish the narrative was a little more concise and clear, but I do appreciate it for what it is.

The visuals and atmosphere are another defining characteristic. The world is something unlike what you find in any other videogame. The art design is absolutely stunning, especially after you leave the initial area which is a bit bland. The creativity and imagination required to create a world like this must be impressive. There are no words for the atmosphere and visuals other than its something you have to experience yourself. There are areas that feel so much like you're in a dream state, yet they are fully explorable.

Overall, this game is fantastic. Again, this is coming from someone who thinks Souls games are terrible. This is among my favorite games of all time. I encourage anyone who gives this game a shot to really tough it out through the initial learning curve because the payoff is absolutely worth it. Its a game that you are in no hurry to complete, and just experiencing the world is part of the enjoyment.

This is a major weakness of souls, obfuscating too much the story and quests to the point in which you either give in to the online wikis or completely ignore questlines. I've had a bit of both in this game. I'm okay with consulting a wiki from time to time to better make my decisions, but this is just too much.Summary: I'd rather have a semi open-world, featuring half the length of this one with the more trascendental and impactful moments and putting more thought in accessibility and better informing the players to help them take their decisions regarding build and quests. items.quote:
As a fan of the Souls series, I got into Elden Ring with much hype and excitement which, at first, was rewarded. It has the right atmosphere and the right feeling to be exactly what I wanted.
But, for me, the open world formula did not really work for this kind of game. I found myself exploring areas that became tedious and unrewarding, having the story fragmented and less compelling. And the world overall seemed just too large. I like to play this kind of games by always defeating each enemy at least once in order to consider an area "cleared". And in Elden Ring this was a Sisyphean task, very unrewarding and it eventually ate away at my enjoyment.
Elden Ring is probably a great game for people who wanted something different or, from what I've talked about with friends, for people ho haven't played previous Souls games and had no expectations from it. But for me, as I said earlier, the open world formula did not really do it. I've played it for 100+ hours and still didn't finish the story. But, by that point, I didn't really want to anymore.

items.quote: Elden Ring is a breathtakingly ambitious collaboration between FromSoftware and George R.R. Martin that exceeds all expectations. This action-packed RPG is an absolute triumph, blending the unparalleled genius of Hidetaka Miyazaki's game design with Martin's unparalleled storytelling prowess, creating an experience that is truly **** its core, Elden Ring is a celebration of the very best aspects of the Dark Souls series, while also pushing boundaries to deliver an entirely new and captivating adventure. The world-building is a work of pure art, with each intricate environment meticulously crafted to the finest detail. From the vast open fields to the foreboding dungeons, every corner of the map holds surprises and secrets that make exploration both thrilling and **** combat in Elden Ring is as brutal and satisfying as one would expect from a FromSoftware game. Each encounter is a dance of life and death, requiring precise timing, strategic thinking, and patience. The addition of mounted combat adds a new layer of excitement, allowing players to engage in epic battles with colossal enemies, creating moments that are nothing short of **** of the standout features of Elden Ring is its engrossing narrative. George R.R. Martin's involvement shines through, infusing the game with his signature mastery of storytelling. The lore is rich, mysterious, and filled with memorable characters that leave a lasting impact. The dialogue and world-building are Shakespearean, with every interaction feeling weighty and meaningful.Furthermore, Elden Ring boasts an exceptional soundtrack that perfectly complements each moment, enhancing the emotional impact of every scene. The haunting melodies and thunderous orchestrations add an extra layer of immersion, making every triumph or setback feel all the more potent.While Elden Ring is undoubtedly a masterpiece, it does have a few minor flaws. Occasionally, the game's difficulty can feel overwhelming, especially for newcomers to the genre. The learning curve may be steep, but the sense of accomplishment that comes with conquering these challenges is well worth the effort.

items.quote:
Elden Ring is a good game - period, but I feel it lost something compared to previous games from FromSoftware. 
First the good stuff, gorgeous art direction, snappy combat with a lot of playstyle to suit your fantasy(but unfortunately not so balanced), breathtaking moments in vista discovery, and some of the best legacy dungeons.
Now for the bad stuff, this feels like a wikipedia game, I couldn't finish even a sidequest, and I missed a lot of content that felt too important in my first playthrough like Malenia. I don't think that is good design.  Then there are the recycled bosses.. urgh, DS1 had a handful of bosses but they feel much more impactful and memorable. Also final boss wasn't that memorable, and rather frustrating.
The open world aspects offer a lot of awe and amazement but also can break the game due to over leveling, under leveling can be ok, sure, but damn defeating a story boss on your first time diminishes the importance of these mythical beings. And talking about some story aspects, I find it hard to connect. It's cryptic in a way that doesn't help it compared to the other souls likes. I felt like a psychopathic outsider who arrived in a world just to kill everything. 
I genuinely root for FromSoftware and I love their games that's why I am so critical of every detail in Elden Ring. I hope they learned a lot with their first open world and we will see even a better game with the sequel.

items.quote:
It is hard for me to even put into words how incredible this game is. As a huge Dark Souls fan and someone who loves open world/exploration focused game, this is perfection. Stunningly beautiful landscapes. Punishing and mechanically complex boss fights. This game has it all and even after 3 full playthroughs, I still find myself getting drawn back in to play a new way on a regular basis

Everyone experiences games differently, some people enjoy the punishment and others don't (I do lol). You can go through the game without using your mount or a summon in tougher areas and get a true Souls experience, but with a whole host of options for summoning and making your character more powerful leading up to boss fights, this is also the most accessible entry to date. If you have been on the fence about a Souls game, this is the one to try.

This game is a 10 for me and while it is my ideal game... its not without flaws and also is definitely not a game for everyone. I've tried really hard to find complaints about the game but most of them have been fixed by now and they're so nit-picky that its not even worth it to me. I waited for this game since they announced it in 2017 and it came through in every aspect.

items.quote:
Elden Ring è una straordinaria esperienza open world che cattura **** fin dal primo istante. Con un vasto mondo da esplorare, ricco e "denso" di contenuti e molteplici attività da intraprendere, questo gioco offre un'esperienza di gioco fenomale.

Grafica e Ambientazione (7/10) Una delle prime cose che colpiscono del gioco è la sua ambientazione curata nel dettaglio. Il mondo di gioco è ricco di paesaggi mozzafiato, dalla maestosità delle montagne alla bellezza dei boschi, il tutto reso con una cura incredibile per i dettagli. L'unico "pecca" è che il comparto tecnico non all'altezza del periodo attuale, fortunatamente ciò non intacca la fruizione del contenuto in quanto comunque è ben ottimizzato garantendo così un'esperienza molto fluida a qualsiasi risoluzione.

Gameplay (9.5/10) Il gameplay ovviamente è il punto di forza del gioco come tutti i contenuti di From Software. La libertà di esplorazione è illimitata, e puoi scegliere come affrontare le sfide che il mondo ti propone. La quest line principale è abbastanza intuitiva in quanto il gioco ti "indirizza" attraverso un sistema di navigazione leggerissimo vicino alle grazie, non al massimo della intuitività ma neanche incomprensibile, mentre tutte le varie quest "secondarie" nonostante siano state sviluppate in maniera eccelsa sono molto complesse sia da trovare che completare, se vai avanti con la quest principale alcune potresti addirittura perderle. Un po' di game loop si avverte con i boss opzionali che trovi in giro nella mappa, problematica smorzata in quanto nonostante siano uguali hanno un pattern di abilità differente (lievemente). Il resto è magia, il mondo di gioco è ricco di contenuti e segreti, esplorarlo è fantastico e mai ripetitivo/noioso.

Longevità (10 /10) Potresti letteralmente giocarci all'infinito per provare le varie build e fare diverse run o semplicemente per scoprire tutto il gioco senza l'ausilio di guide online.

Conclusione

In sintesi, non darei un 10 perché il gioco non è perfetto, qualche piccola carenza ce l'ha, carenze che per me sono completamente ignorabili e presenti in qualsiasi gioco esistente. 9.5 è il mio voto finale! Grazie From Software

items.quote: This "Souls: Big World" game seems like a step back from Dark Souls and Bloodborne. Sure, the world looks nice and mounted combat is fun... But it all gets old really quick. The story is meh, the music is just a few notes on repeat. There are a few good bosses, but nothing comes close to Gael and Kos. Sure, Malenia is challenging and forces you to adapt, but beating her isn't as satisfactory, as her anime flurry attacks make her look like a clown. I think it's pretty obvious that most of the critics didn't finish the game but played it for a dozen hours or so and gave it a 10/10. I you really put your time into this game and compare it to predecessors, its flaws become painfully obvious. Oh, and the camera and AI are still complete ****. From really sold out with this generic open world game, you would think they would at least be bothered to patch Bloodborne to 60 FPS after almost 10 years. Maybe they should be mandated to play Bloodborne again. Perhaps it would help them remember what a great game actually looks like. I really did not want From turning into Bethesda, but here we are. SMH.

items.quote:
My benchmarks:
- Visual: 5/5
- Music: 4/5
- Gameplay: 5/5
- Map Design: 3/5

Overall: 4.5/5

The best Souls game yet from Fromsoft. 

Lots of improvements in gameplay from previous Souls games, ranging from dedicated jump button to refined dual stance from DS2.

Visual and art direction is phenomenal, as well as beautiful soundtracks.

Map design is a mixed bag, however. While the overworld design is very intricate and carefully crafted, the various secret mini dungeons are bland and repetitive. The reuse many main bosses and mini bosses later on in the game is also very lazy on their part. Frankly speaking, the secret dungeons feel like fillers most of the time, and the game would be better off without them.

items.quote:
I am honestly perplexed when I hear people say they put over 120+ hours into this game. The exploration just didn't do it for me like other open world titles. 

Don't get me wrong, for the first 20 hours I was having a blast exploring and figuring out my build, but it quickly started to become repetitive and tedious for me. I became so bored with fighting random grunt enemies that I just started running past every one of them I saw. It's less that the enemies were hard to kill, and more that they took too much time and were too similar to each other. I mean the interactions mostly play out the same every damn time; I wait out there attacks, go in for the kill, rinse repeat for the other 50 enemies in the vicinity. I just kept thinking to myself that I would so much rather be fighting the boss. So caves for me quickly became a sprint fest trying to find the reward, boss room, or any useful items on the ground. Then the reward wouldn't fit my build so I wasted my time.... well at least the bosses were usually cool I guess.

The over world exploration is also very hit or miss, there are many places you just can't get to without doing some random event or finding a hidden warp gate (I hate the warp gates). I remember there was one high plateau in Liurnia of the Lakes that I tried to get to for like 25 minutes before I gave in and looked up how to get there. As it turned out, I couldn't get up there at that point of the game. That isn't good open world design in my opinion; it's limiting. 

The quests and NPC's often feel disjointed. I get that the developers didn't want to hold your hand, but I feel they went too far. Some sort of indication where NPC's new locations are after teleporting, or a general direction you should be going for a quest would be nice.

Even with all that said, I still greatly enjoyed the experience. The strongest suit to this game is the opening 20-30 hours. I would say all the bosses I fought up to Morgot were awesome. Even the optional ones were generally fun, albeit a bit easy at times. Margit and Godrick are amazing first bosses because they are challenging but fair. Their moves have pretty obvious telegraphs, but I still found myself losing over and over. Learning to fight them was a blast. I personally went into the Godrick fight a bit under-leveled, but it was still a rewarding experience nonetheless. The spectacle of the bosses was also amazing-- a special nod to the voice actors and ost for making the fights that much better.

If the game ended after Morgott (or generally close), I probably would have given the game an 8. The whole time I was playing the game, I saw that giant tree in the background. It was such an awesome image always visible from everywhere in the over-world. Then I finally made my way through the capital city, reached the throne, and approached the foot of the tree. Then the game sent me off somewhere else for multiple hours....... WHY? It was so anticlimactic for me. I hated the Mountaintops of the the Giants and that crappy tornado place. The enemies in the snow area are all re-used and annoyingly beefy. The enemies in tornado town are just plain annoying... 

Also, I think the last handful of bosses are terribly imbalanced. I know there are cheese methods to beat them, but I always fought 1 on 1 with bosses. It really felt like Fromsoftware was begging me to use a summon in these fights, during Melenia especially. Melenia is the culmination of the unbalanced design of the endgame. Her entire "Difficulty" is dodging that one attack she does with the crazy slashes. Every other move in the game gives you a good idea of how to dodge it. NOT THAT ONE THO. This was the first time I've ever had to look up a tutorial on how to dodge one move. Even when I finally did beat her, I didn't feel good. Most of the time when I beat a hard boss I have that moment of euphoria where I feel triumphant; not with Melenia though. I spam rolled through her waterfowl and just got lucky eventually... what a letdown of a fight. It **** too because Melenia seems like she would be awesome. Who doesn't love a cool bad-ass swords-woman character?

As a last note, I also tried new game plus. I wish there was a way to just replay the bosses instead. I don't want to run all over the map just to fight the bosses again, it's boring. In a linear game, replaying it would be much less of an issue. In Elden Ring it takes so long just to get from one area to another.

Overall, not my favorite open world game. I did get 70 hours of playtime out of it so I am not too mad with the experience. Again, would probably have been an 8 for me if not for the last stretch of the game.
items.author: Rapta

items.quote:
Although many may complain that action wise, Elden Ring did not bring anything new to the table, there is no denying that action is still very much rewarding and fun. From Software seems to have soften up on their stance, albeit in a much more clever way, of not including an easy mode. To be fair, over leveling can be considered an "easy mode" or having someone help you, which has always been available through the souls series can always be an easy mode. But now with the spirit bell, ashes of war, and TONS of different OP weapons, it can easily be said that FS has now incorporated an easy mode.

Now for the elephant in the room, the open world aspect. Fantastically done and quite expansive. I have about 400 hours at the time of this review and in my 4th play through and I still find stuff I didn't find before. Talk about bang for your buck. The best $60 I have spent in a longtime. 

My only complaints and nitpicks is something I have been crying about since all of the souls games and that is the lackluster facial talking animations. At least they are somewhat putting an effort in where the mouths actually move when the characters speak but it is so rudimentary that for a triple A studio, it is pretty embarrassing. I also thought that some of the dungeons were a bit repetitive, something Miyazaki admitted was a failure on Bloodborne's chalice dungeons which made it surprising that he repeated his mistake. They needed to have a bit more flair to them and something surprising but they were all pretty much the same. 

Wonderful entry into the souls series and if you have never played a souls game I would suggest starting with this one as it is by far the most approachable for all of its "easy mode" options.

items.quote: I played this game in early 2023, and it was my first FromSoftware game. I really enjoyed the main story, although I had to watch a lot of videos to fully grasp it.
